📋 12 Entry Points

Enforcement

Enforcement Powers — Criminal Sanctions, Prosecution, Penalties

DWI enforcement framework — Water Industry Act 1991. Criminal prosecution for supply failures. Enforcement notices. Improvement plans. Financial penalties — Water Services Regulation Authority (Ofwat). Prosecution for water quality failures. DWI Chief Inspector annual report. Statutory duty to supply wholesome water. Emergency prohibitions. Boil water notices.

Monitoring

Compliance Monitoring — Sampling, Testing, Reporting

Water quality monitoring programme — 4.8M samples annually. Chemical, microbiological, aesthetic parameters. DWI audit of water company laboratories. Sampling frequency requirements. Compliance assessment — individual and system compliance. Investigative monitoring for failures. Customer contact trigger sampling. Emergency response sampling. Third-party laboratory accreditation (UKAS).

PFAS

PFAS Monitoring — Forever Chemicals, Risk Assessment

Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) — emerging contaminant class. Drinking water standard: 100ng/l aggregate. PFAS source identification — firefighting foam, industrial discharge. Water company PFAS monitoring programme. Treatment technology assessment — GAC, ion exchange, RO. Risk assessment for catchment areas. International comparison — EU, US EPA standards. PFAS health effects research integration.

Lead

Lead Pipe Replacement — Programme, Compliance, Funding

Lead pipe replacement programme — target: all lead pipes replaced by 2050. Estimated 6-10M lead service pipes in England and Wales. Water company investment programme — AMP8. Customer engagement — lead awareness, free testing. Lead monitoring — 25 µg/l action level, 10 µg/l target. Phosphate dosing as interim measure. Priority areas — schools, hospitals, childcare. Funding mechanisms — Ofwat, water company investment.

Private Supplies

Private Supplies — Regulation, Risk Assessment, Enforcement

Private water supplies — 97,000+ in England. Local authority regulation. Risk assessment programme — Type A (commercial), Type B (single dwelling), Type C (large). Monitoring requirements by risk category. Enforcement notices. Treatment requirements. Funding — private supply grants. Tenant protection. Agricultural contamination risk. Legionella risk. EU Drinking Water Directive alignment.

Cyber

Cyber Security — Operational Technology, SCADA, Resilience

Water sector cyber security — NCSC guidance. Operational technology (OT) protection — SCADA, PLCs, telemetry. Supply chain cyber risk. Incident reporting — NCSC, ICO. Resilience testing. Network segmentation. Legacy system security. IT/OT convergence risks. NIS Regulations compliance. National Security Act implications. Water company cyber maturity assessment.

Resilience

Supply Resilience — Drought, Flooding, Infrastructure

Water supply resilience — drought planning, demand management. Infrastructure resilience — treatment works, reservoirs, distribution network. Climate change adaptation — rainfall patterns, demand growth. Emergency supply planning — tankers, bowsers, alternative sources. Cross-border supply agreements. Water transfer schemes. Strategic resource options. Regional resilience assessment. Consumer conservation campaigns.

Companies

Water Company Performance — Ofwat, Consumer, Standards

Water company performance framework — Ofwat price review (PR24). Service incentive mechanism (SIM). Customer experience metrics. Financial resilience. Environmental performance — pollution incidents, leakage. Asset health. Innovation funding — Ofwat Innovation Fund. Retail market competition. Developer services. Water poverty. Vulnerability register. Consumer Council for Water (CCW).

Treatment

Treatment Technology — Innovation, Standards, Investment

Treatment technology review — conventional, advanced, emerging. Cryptosporidium treatment — ozone, UV. Disinfection by-product management. Taste and odour control. Microplastic removal. PFAS treatment — GAC, ion exchange. Manganese and iron treatment. Water treatment works optimization. Chemical dosing management. Sludge treatment. Energy efficiency in treatment.

Network

Distribution Network — Quality, Leakage, Asset Health

Distribution network management — water quality deterioration in network. Leakage — national target 50% reduction by 2050. Asset health monitoring — pipe age, material, failure rate. Pressure management. Discolouration risk. Biofilm management. Metering programme. DMA (District Metered Area) management. Smart network sensors. Real-time quality monitoring. Pipe rehabilitation techniques.

Data

Data Governance — Quality, Open Data, Analytics

Water quality data management — 4.8M+ samples annually. Open data publication — DWI annual report, company returns. Real-time monitoring data. Consumer complaint data. Incident data. Water company regulatory returns. Data quality assurance. Interoperability — common data standards. Water quality modelling. Predictive analytics. Digital twin development for distribution networks.

Parliamentary

Parliamentary Evidence — Reform, Scrutiny, Standards

DWI Chief Inspector annual report to Parliament. EFRA Committee scrutiny — water quality, company performance. PQ evidence — PFAS, lead pipes, private supplies, leakage. Water (Special Measures) Bill. Consumer protection evidence. Environmental standards. Industry reform recommendations. Privatisation review evidence. Regional comparison. International benchmarking.

Automated sampling trigger. Consumer alert system. Integration with treatment works SCADA. Target: 95% network coverage by 2028, contamination detection from days to minutes, 80% reduction in boil water incidents.

2. PFAS Intelligence Platform

AI-powered PFAS source identification — catchment risk mapping, industrial discharge tracking. Predictive PFAS transport modelling. Treatment effectiveness monitoring. Compliance dashboard against 100ng/l standard. International benchmark tracking. Health risk assessment integration. Target: 100% PFAS monitoring compliance, treatment optimisation for 50 highest-risk supplies, catchment-level PFAS reduction strategy.

AI-optimised lead pipe replacement programme — priority area identification, cost modelling, customer engagement scheduling. Predictive lead risk scoring — property age, pipe material, sampling data. Target: Lead pipe replacement rate tripled by 2028, 100% high-priority (schools, hospitals) replaced by 2027.

Treatment recommendation engine. Local authority enforcement tracker. Tenant protection alerts. Environmental performance scoring. Consumer outcome tracking. Cross-company benchmarking. Target: Real-time performance monitoring for all 17 water companies in England and Wales, predictive company risk assessment quarterly.

Target: 100% SCADA coverage with AI monitoring, mean time to detect cyber incidents under 1 hour, NIS Regulations compliance for all companies.

7. Drought and Flood Resilience

Predictive demand modelling — weather, population, economic growth. AI drought trigger management. Water transfer optimisation. Emergency supply logistics. Target: 20% reduction in per-capita consumption by 2030, drought resilience for all regions, automated emergency supply activation.

8. Parliamentary Intelligence Platform

Automated DWI reporting — annual report, PQ evidence, EFRA Committee briefing. Real-time water quality dashboard for MPs. Constituency-level water quality data. PFAS hotspot mapping. Lead pipe replacement progress by constituency. Consumer complaint trends. Target: Quarterly automated parliamentary briefing packs, constituency-level water quality data for all 650 MPs.

🚫 Red Lines (Never Crossed)

  • ❌ No water quality data suppressed or delayed without DWI Chief Inspector authorisation — every contamination event must be reported within statutory timeframe, no exceptions for commercial sensitivity
  • ❌ No private supply owner penalised without prior risk assessment and advisory period — enforcement must follow risk-based graduated approach: advice → notice → enforcement
  • ❌ No PFAS standard relaxation without Parliamentary approval — the 100ng/l aggregate standard is statutory; any change requires legislative process and public consultation
  • ❌ No automated enforcement action without human DWI inspector review — AI may flag compliance issues but every enforcement notice must be issued by a qualified inspector
  • ❌ No consumer data shared beyond regulatory requirements — sampling results, complaint data, and metering data governed by UK GDPR and Water Industry Act data powers
  • ❌ No water company cyber vulnerability disclosed beyond NCSC and Ofwat — cyber security data is sensitive infrastructure information; publication requires national security assessment
